recentItems.title: Many no-shows on first days of new booking system for scenic HK hiking trail
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hong Kong authorities will review a new reservation system for a Sai Kung trail famed for its dramatic volcanic rock columns after the National Day “golden week” in October, following large numbers of no-shows during the first two trial runs. Only 1,560 registered and walk-in patrons arrived at Po Pin Chau on Saturday and Sunday, despite 3,230 people having made bookings under the real-name reservation system. Lawmakers and a district councillor have called for more on-site quotas, clearer booking status information for walk-ins, and a penalty-points system to curb no-shows.

recentItems.title: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatoa covers cities in volcanic ash
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Indonesia’s Anak Krakatoa volcano erupted continuously for three days, beginning with an initial blast late Friday night. The nation’s meteorological agency reported two significant eruptions on Sunday that sent volcanic ash more than 150km (83 miles) away and across five provinces. Residents in the capital Jakarta were among those finding homes and cars covered in ashfall. Eight airports in the country were forced to suspend operations, stranding more than 170,000 passengers.

recentItems.title: International media allowed in China’s Gyirong Port
recentItems.description:
Chinese authorities announced on Sunday that search teams have retrieved 12 additional bodies, as efforts persist to locate hundreds who remain unaccounted for following the glacial collapse and subsequent massive flash flood that devastated China's primary border crossing with Nepal. Forty-three people have been confirmed dead and 519 remain missing on the Chinese side 11 days after the disaster. The announcement came as a small contingent of foreign media were allowed to visit the port for the first time since the deadly flash floods.

recentItems.title: Amazon cargo jet in deadly crash in Florida
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane shot off a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, striking multiple vehicles before bursting into flames. The crash happened at around 2pm local time in the US state of Florida, forcing the temporary closure of one of the country’s busiest airports. Officials said five other people were injured and sent to hospital. Some of the victims including the pilot and co-pilot of the jet were trapped and had to be rescued. Firefighters also had to contain a fuel leak after the crash.

recentItems.title: Dignity and dialysis: The hospital where patients earn a living while getting life-saving care
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

On the fourth storey of a haemodialysis centre in the Chinese city of Guangzhou, chronic kidney disease patients have formed a community to stitch clothes to make a living. Many of them lost their jobs after being diagnosed with end-stage renal disease, or uraemia. Unable to afford kidney transplants, they will need dialysis treatments three times a week for the rest of their lives. Baoshutang Haemodialysis Centre co-founder Dr Xie Qiang said the factory is a beacon of hope for his patients.

recentItems.title: Two rescued in Nepal 10 days after disaster
recentItems.description:
Two people, including a Chinese national, have been rescued 10 days after a glacial collapse caused a catastrophic flash flood disaster on the China-Nepal border. Lu Haitao, a Chinese national, became trapped in a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district. He was rescued on Saturday by the Nepalese army. Aside from showing mild signs of hypothermia, Lu had no visible injuries and his vitals were stable. Another survivor, 64-year-old Chandra Shrestha, was found alive in the debris of her partially buried home. She was airlifted to a hospital in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, for treatment.

recentItems.title: How Starbucks Malaysia changed the game for deaf baristas
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A decade ago, Starbucks Malaysia launched an ambitious experiment to create meaningful career opportunities for the nation’s deaf community. The initiative evolved from offering entry-level jobs into establishment of the world’s first Starbucks Signing Store in Kuala Lumpur. Now, deaf employees are even able to build long-term careers and advance to management roles. As the pilot project changed lives, the concept was expanded to 26 stores around the world. But despite the programme’s success, major communication and educational barriers remain for disabled people hoping to enter the mainstream workforce.

recentItems.title: Why does Hong Kong struggle to ease competition among its youth?
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

More on Hong Kong education: https://sc.mp/19c5a5

Since Hong Kong’s handover in 1997, the government has sought to transform the city’s education system from a colonial system focused on memorisation and exam pressure, and towards a more holistic development meant to foster lifelong learning. But decades on, competition has only grown stronger among Hong Kong’s young students, extending beyond the confines of the classroom and into their extracurricular activities. What are the factors driving this competition and what is being done to ease pressure on pupils?

recentItems.title: Hong Kong caps access to Sai Kung trail with reservation scheme
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more: https://sc.mp/4e43e4

Hong Kong authorities are capping access to a popular Sai Kung trail starting Saturday. Visitor numbers on the coastal Po Pin Chau section of the High Island Geo Trail will be limited to 2,000 per day on weekends and public holidays. Hikers planning to visit during these times will need to register in advance. The initiative marks Hong Kong’s first countryside crowd-control scheme.
